text:
Priya (CS): Morning — quick weekly sync for Corvus. Focus: caching + batching effectiveness after last week's micro-config changes. High level: usage +12% w/w, p95 latency ~310ms, error rate spiking to ~0.9% during 13:00–14:30 UTC, and spend up ~8%. Can we confirm hit rate / batch size impact?

cache-bot: automated metrics dump for Corvus (past 24h):
```
prefix_cache_hit_rate=0.47
kv_cache_hitrate=0.61
avg_batch_size=3.7
median_batch_size=3
95pct_batch_size=7
p50_latency=220ms
p95_latency=310ms
errors_total=42 (0.9%)
cost_per_1k_tokens=$3.95
requests_per_min_peak=920
```

Marco (SRE): Thanks Priya — seeing the same in our traces. The error spikes are correlated with a spike in short, single-turn requests that bypass prefix cache and push batches to small sizes. We saw queue backpressure on a subset of nodes 13:05–13:22 UTC. Logs show some `BatchTimeout` retries.

Evan (Eng): Noted. The micro-config change increased `max_batch_window_ms` from 20 -> 40 and lowered `min_batch_size` to 2 to reduce latency for interactive users. That improved median latency but allowed many 1-2 request batches during peak which hurts throughput/cost.

Renee (Solutions Eng): Customer feedback: Corvus loves lower p50 but noticed higher invoices and occasional timeouts in the integration test suite. They're asking if we can preserve their interactive latency wins while improving hit rate / cost.

Priya (CS): Goal: keep p50 <= 250ms for their core flow, push p95 below 300ms ideally, and raise prefix hit rate >= 0.6 without increasing cost > current baseline. Any tactical config suggestions we can roll today?

Marco (SRE): Tactical idea: enable small client-side jitter and a short aggregation window at the ingress (client 10–15ms) to allow micro-batching without adding user-facing latency. On server side: set `min_batch_size=3` and `max_batch_window_ms=30` for Corvus route. That should nudge average batch size up from ~3.7 to ~4.5 during peaks.

Evan (Eng): I can patch the route config. Proposed diff (snippet):
```yaml
routes:
  corvus-main:
    batching:
      enabled: true
      min_batch_size: 3
      max_batch_window_ms: 30
    caching:
      prefix_enabled: true
      prefix_ttl_s: 300
      kv_cache_size: 20000
```
I'll stage in a canary to 10% of traffic for 30m then roll if green.

Renee (Solutions Eng): Also recommend we enable selective prefix caching for their high-cardinality prompt templates only — avoids cache pollution. I'll send the list of 6 templates to whitelist.

Priya (CS): Nice. Can we estimate expected delta on cost / hit rate? Approx numbers ok.

cache-bot: quick projection based on sim (30% traffic with patched config):
```
expected_prefix_hit_rate=0.58 -> 0.63
avg_batch_size=3.7 -> 4.6
proj_cost_per_1k_tokens=$3.95 -> $3.45 (-12.7%)
proj_p95_latency=310ms -> 295ms
```

Marco (SRE): We should also enable a fallback lane: if batch size < 2 after window, route to low-latency small-instance pool to avoid retry cascades. That reduces timeouts at tail.

Evan (Eng): Will add fallback rule and the canary. Roll plan: 10% 30m -> 30% 1h -> 100% 2h with rollback on errors >0.6% or p95 > 320ms.

Renee (Solutions Eng): I'll coordinate the whitelist and share a small customer-facing note explaining the canary and expected savings so Corvus doesn't get surprised.

Priya (CS): Action items: Evan to open config PR + canary (ETA 2h), Marco to set SRE alert for BatchTimeout and node queue depth, Renee to send template whitelist and customer note, I'll update Corvus and schedule a short sync after 2h canary.

Evan (Eng): PR up: https://git.redwood/infra/patches/2348 — canary scheduled in 15m.

Marco (SRE): Alert created: `corvus.batch_timeout_rate` threshold 0.5% (5m). Also added temporary additional pod headroom during canary.

Renee (Solutions Eng): Whitelist sent to Priya via email. Customer note draft: "We'll be running a short canary to improve batching and caching — expected 10–15% cost reduction and slightly better p95. We'll monitor and pause if any regressions."

Priya (CS): Great. We'll reconvene after the canary window. :thumbsup:
